scenes.heading: EXT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL FOR BOYS - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Snow falls on the darkened school...
Long weekends at the Longborough School for
Boys were a quiet time, as most children went
home to their families.
We find the ONLY window with a LIGHT ON.

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL - DORM ROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Space has been made for a large card table in the center of the
room. YOUNG NED sits with FOUR 10-year-old BOYS.
There were those students, however, who
gathered not out of friendship, but because
they had nowhere else to go.
They look to the head of the table where--
INGMAR TODD
A severe-looking 10 year old, with the serious, professional
manner of a Monte Carlo croupier, opens a slick case revealing a
beautiful, tabletop-sized roulette wheel.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Ingmar Todd was the son of roving
missionaries. He had arrived at boarding
school with a professionally-certified and
balanced roulette wheel.
The boys lean back as Ingmar sweeps out a rolled-up felt
roulette number grid, carefully picks some lint from it.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As there was very little else to do, Ingmar’s
room became a center of activity.
The boys excitedly place their bets on the grid. Some quarters,
various odd trinkets and candies.
Young Ned places some individually-wrapped golden chocolates on
the grid, a few on numbers, a bunch on Black and some on Red.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
All Young Ned had to wager was the box of
chocolates he’d hastily snuck into his
suitcase the day his father dropped him off
at boarding school.
Ingmar sets the ball rolling around the edge...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It often occurred to Young Ned that had his
mother lived, she would not have deserted him
like his father.
On Young Ned as he watches the ball go in circles...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
She would have known how to comfort him, and
help him grieve for his loss. But as it was
his mother who had died, this was a circular
logic that got him nowhere.
Young Ned notices his EMPTY CHOCOLATE BOX has a small folded
card tucked in the wrapping and ribbon. He opens it--
ANGLE - THE CARD
“To my little ‘Big Daddy.’ Just for being a great boy. [heart]
Mom.”
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It was then he realized the individually-
wrapped chocolates, currently in play, had been
intended as a gift to him from his mother, for
an occasion which had never arrived.
Ingmar lifts his hand, signaling--
(accent)
Bets are closed.
A distressed Young Ned studies the board.
WAY UP CLOSE TO THE SILVER BALL
We TRAVEL with it around the wheel until... BALL RESTS on “00.”
INGMAR (CONT’D)
Double zed. House wins.
Young Ned looks confused as Ingmar uses his polished wooden
stick to sweep the felt clean of all the booty.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED: (2)
Like many beginning players, Young Ned bet on
both Red and Black, but failed to consider the
double zero on the wheel. He lost everything.
As Young Ned watches the other players resume playing, and picks
up his empty chocolate box...
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The lesson was clear: in gambling, no matter
how well you think you know the odds, there’s
always an outcome you can’t see coming.
CLOSE ON THE ROULETTE WHEEL--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
During the years that followed, the Pie-Maker
avoided taking gambles, with a few, notable
exceptions.
MATCH CUT TO:
A PIE
Sits baking in the oven.
He invested his life savings in a bakery at a
time when carbohydrates had fallen completely
out of fashion, and more importantly...
The oven door opens to REVEAL CHUCK peering in. She pulls the
pie from the oven, and we’re--

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - KITCHEN - DAY

lines.text: As Chuck drops a slice of pie on a plate--
...he had gambled on the love of his childhood
sweetheart, the girl next door who had
returned from the dead.
NED is startled as Chuck uses a LONG TOASTING FORK to thrust a
forkful of pie under his nose.
Try this.
Like the fork.
Like being alive.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
He takes the bite.
CHUCK (CONT’D)
It’s a new flavor we could serve, Spring
passion fruit. And I know it’s not Spring,
but it is in New Zealand, which makes it
exotic and upside-down which is how we could
serve it.
Betting on Chuck had made the Pie-Maker
happier than he had ever been.
We’ll put it on the menu.
I like Daring Ned.
It seems since you arrived, Cautious Ned has
left the building.
OLIVE enters.
Who’s the new guy at the counter? The
handsome, brooding, older man with a sensual
twinkle? Plus, he smells good.
Olive nods her head and they look out the circle to:
DWIGHT, 50, handsome, seated at the counter, wearing a suit.
He mumbled something odd to me earlier.
There was no word that completely described
the feeling the square-shouldered older man
had given the Pie-Maker.
Do you ever shiver when you pee? Because
that’s how I felt when he spoke...
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA - FLASHBACK TO MOMENTS EARLIER

lines.text: As Ned passes Dwight at the counter...
More coffee?
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED:
This pie is delicious. As good as your mother’s.
Ned pauses, a little shiver. He moves on--
BACK TO SCENE
Chuck is instantly intrigued. As they continue to watch him eat
from the circle...
He said that? Did he know your mother?
I didn’t ask. A stranger says a strange thing
in passing, chances are I misheard him, or
misunderstood. Maybe when he said my
“mother’s” pie, he didn’t mean my mother, he
meant everyone’s mother -- the iconic, all-
American mother created by advertisers and
politicians as a shorthand for “family values”
and a longing for baked goods.
Would that make you shiver?
If someone knew something about my family, that
would give me the piss-jitters. But I’d ask
them about it, not hide in the kitchen.
I’m not hiding.
Dwight looks up at them and they pull back from the circle
window, leaving Olive in view.
I think he’s cute.
(waves, mouths)
Hi.
(to Ned)
If the nice-smelling man has something to
share about your family, I want to know.
So do I.
OFF this...
DINING AREA - MOMENTS LATER
Ned approaches Dwight.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED:
I’m probably making a mountain out of a molehill
over a random comment I probably misheard? And
I’m hoping to offset any awkwardness you are or
will be feeling by providing your slice of three-
plum on the house.
You’re a nervous talker. Like your dad.
Dwight smiles, Ned freezes.
This complicates things. You may have to pay
for the pie.
(shakes Ned’s hand)
Dwight Dixon. I was best friends with your
father 25 years ago. You are Ned, am I right?
The Pie-Maker considered the strange stranger,
and his estranged father. And lied.
Nope.
Chuck and Olive step up, preventing Ned’s exit.
Yes you are, silly. And I’m Olive.
And I’m--
(off their look)
Kitty. Kitty Pimms. You knew Ned’s parents?
Back when they were dating. Was the peak of
peach season when they met. She baked a brown
sugar crust, your dad didn’t have a chance.
Don’t remember them mentioning you.
I was in the service with your dad, back before
you were born. Your pops didn’t like to
reminisce. Probably a lot he didn’t talk about.
Sounds familiar.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED: (2)
Thing is, I’m trying to find him and I
thought maybe you could help? Love to see
him again.
(then)
You got his face, you know. ‘Specially around
the eyes.
The Pie-Maker had hoped never to be likened to
his father, whether it be around the eyes...
I’m afraid we lost touch.
...or the heart.
About 20 years ago.
Shame. Any thoughts on where I might look--
No and while you’re obviously speaking from a
good and helpful place, it’s not good and
helpful. To me.
Didn’t mean to stir anything up. I’ll be in
town for a few days, you change your mind...
But Ned’s moved on. On Chuck, watching him go:
As Chuck marveled at the Pie-Maker’s refusal
to help search for his only parent...

scenes.heading: INT. EMERSON’S OFFICE - DAY

lines.text: Emerson has his feet up on his desk, happily eating Chinese food
from a take-out container.
...Emerson Cod marveled at the digestive coma
produced by beef balls and curried cuttlefish
from the dim sum restaurant downstairs.
He packs up the food containers, throws them away, grabs the
fortune cookie and happily moves to plop on his couch...
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
His phone silenced, Emerson knew the world of
clients and murders would soon be lost in the
cloud of a power nap.
Emerson breaks open his fortune cookie and reads the fortune.
He immediately sits back up, annoyed.
What the hell?
INSERT - THE FORTUNE
Scrawled by hand, it reads: “HELP ME EMERSON COD.” Emerson
SIGHS and stands back up.

scenes.heading: EXT. EMERSON’S OFFICE / DIM SUM BUILDING - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: SINK DOWNWARD from Emerson’s office window to find the
restaurant downstairs--
Arriving downstairs in search of a new case...

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM RESTAURANT - LOBBY - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Red velvet walls with murals of dragons and cranes. WAITRESSES
and BUSBOYS in traditional uniforms. As Emerson enters, looking
around...
...the P.I. stumbled on one from his past.
A CLICKING sound causes Emerson to jump involuntarily to
attention. He turns, startles at the sight of:
SIMONE HUNDIN, carrying a doggie bag, and with a DOG (BUBBLEGUM,
from “BITCHES”) at her heels as she heads out of the restaurant.
She uses her CLICKER to issue the dog commands.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
This was the gist:
VERY QUICK POPS FROM EXISTING FOOTAGE OF EP. 105, ”BITCHES”:
Showing Emerson meeting Simone Hundin, wrestling with Simone
Hundin and walking off with Simone Hundin.
Simone Hundin, obedience expert and widow of
deceased, polygamous dog breeder, Harold Hundin.
While investigating her husband’s murder,
Emerson and Simone had forged a close bond.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
BACK TO SCENE
She sees him.
Emerson Cod.
Simone. What have you been up to?
It was a friendship that had very nearly, but
not quite, become something more.
Breeding. My Bubblegum’s in heat, it was a
long night. But what a treat bumping into you.
Didn’t know you were a dim sum connoisseur.
Best pork buns in town. My office is
upstairs. It’s a dangerous combination.
Simone takes a pork bun from the bag, holds it out.
Bun?
Really shouldn’t, I just--
CLICK. Emerson snaps to attention, takes the bun.
The Private Investigator considered how his
inescapable desire to be obedient to this
obedience trainer was at once thrilling and
terrifying. Then he remembered his case.
Did you send me a message in a cookie?
Wasn’t me. I find there are more reliable
ways to send a message.
She stares steadily at him, a note of seduction. Emerson
reaches for another pork bun, CLICK--
SIMONE (CONT’D)
Leave it.
(he pulls back)
It’s been a pleasure, Mr. Cod. Perhaps we’ll
cross paths again.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED:
As she walks off, we HEAR a (different) woman WEEPING.
Fortunately, Emerson had a distraction from
his conflicting impulses:

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM RESTAURANT - DINING ROOM - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: A client.
Find LAI DI TING, the source of the weeping, seated at a corner
booth with a CARDBOARD BOX at her feet. Lai Di pulls herself
together as Emerson approaches.
Excuse me, ma’am? I’m Emerson Cod, the
private investigator from upstairs. Did you
by any chance contact me?
I’ve seen your billboards. My name is Lai Di.
“Lady”...
Lai Di. I don’t work here. I’m married to
Bao, the chef.
(off the box)
Picking up some things of his.
If you’re married to the chef, can I say your
husband’s pork buns make me glad to be alive.
Man’s a true artist.
Not anymore. But I’ll hire you to find who
killed him.
OFF Emerson...
The facts were these:

scenes.heading: EXT. CHINATOWN - LATE ‘70S - M.O.S.

lines.text: A KODACHROME SUPER-8 HOME MOVIE of Lai Di and her husband, BAO,
recent arrivals from China, eagerly smiling and waving at the
camera, ecstatic to be there.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED:
Lai Di and her husband, Bao, immigrated from
Beijing with the hope of opening their own
restaurant.

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM - BAO’S PREP ROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Bao, now dressed as a chef, stands in his well-organized private
PREP ROOM, surrounded by shelves of ingredients. He closes the
door of a washing machine-sized COMMERCIAL BUN STEAMER, clicks
on a stopwatch to time the buns. Two young DISHWASHERS stand in
the doorway, watching. Behind them, we see a sliver of a BUSY
KITCHEN.
Bao quickly established himself as the premier
authority on the delicate art of bun steaming.
Bao senses he is being watched and shoots a look at the boys,
who run. Bao pulls a Chinese curtain across the door, and goes
back to work. We SEE him prepare a new round of buns--
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
He demanded privacy while he worked, both to
eliminate distractions and protect his
unique recipes.
CURTAIN is pulled aside as Bao’s daughter, MEI (beautiful, 20s),
in her dim sum uniform, transfers buns to her serving cart.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
But even with his daughter working as a
waitress, Bao could never save enough money
for his own restaurant.

scenes.heading: INT. BEDROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK (OVERHEAD SHOT)

lines.text: Lai Di lies in bed with Bao, who looks worried.
It was after a 16-hour shift that Lai Di had
noticed Bao could not sleep. Something had
him terrified.
Lai Di asks a question in Mandarin: “What’s the matter?”
Bao chose to reply in English:
Pressure.
He rolls over, away from her...
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 12.

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM - BAO’S PREP ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: On a GAUGE labeled “PRESSURE” as it pegs into the red.
Lai Di would remember Bao’s misgiving
as ironic.
Bao has his back to the bun steamer, which starts to SHAKE and
leak STEAM. As Bao looks up, an EXPLOSION. STEAMED BUNS and a
SECTION OF PIPE fly toward us (VERISPEED: SLOWING to SLOW MOTION
and then SPEEDING UP as they whip out of frame) -- STEAM fills
the air as Bao drops.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Police were satisfied Bao’s death had been an
accident, but Lai Di was convinced there had
been foul play.

scenes.heading: INT. MORGUE - LAB - NIGHT

lines.text: Find Bao, lying on a gurney with a WIDE LENGTH OF PIPE IMPALED
THROUGH HIS HEAD. Emerson, Ned and Chuck gaze at Bao’s corpse.
Let’s be delicate. He may not speak English.
And with the pipe the way it is, I don’t know
if he’ll speak at all.
A quiet moment as Ned TOUCHES Bao. His eyes open. SUBTITLE
Chuck’s line.
(gently, in Mandarin)
Hello, Bao. We have a few questions.
(whisper)
You speak Chinese?
A little Cantonese and some Mandarin.
Bao blinks, YELLS, PANICKED, startling the Mod Squad.
AHHHHHHHHH!
CHUCK / EMERSON / NED
AHHHHHHHH!
Bao sits up and turns to look at them, forcing them to stumble
backward, barely avoiding the swinging pipe.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 13.
CONTINUED:
Heads up! Whoa--
(in English)
Please don’t hurt me. I’m sorry I lost the bet.
We don’t want to hurt you.
What bet?
Gambling at the dim sum. Now someone’s going
to kill me...
A moment. They look at him, then:
“Going” to kill you?
More ducking as he looks around the room, hops off the gurney.
I don’t know how they’ll do it, but they’ll do
it for sure.
Who wants to kill you?
And who were you gambling with?
I tell you and I’m a dead man!
(re: the pipe)
What we need is a mirror.
I gotta get outta here--
Bao makes a break for the exam room door.
Bao, no! Wait!
Bao runs, but the pipe is too wide for the doorway. They
grimace as it CLANGS on the doorframe and Bao staggers backward.
Ned touches Bao and he collapses.
Ouch?
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 14.
CONTINUED: (2)
OFF them--
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: EXT. DIM SUM RESTAURANT - NIGHT

lines.text: Emerson walks up to the restaurant on the busy Chinatown street.
As it appeared the bun steamer’s buns were
steamed over a bet at the dim sum, Emerson Cod
returned to the restaurant for a chat with
Bao’s daughter.

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM RESTAURANT - A LITTLE LATER

lines.text: Emerson trails MEI TING (little or no accent), who’s in her dim
sum waitress outfit and hair as she pushes her serving cart
through the restaurant, handing dishes to patrons.
I don’t understand why my mother hired you.
My father’s death was an accident.
Your mother had a hunch. I could gold-leaf my
bathroom with what I make off mother-hunches.
And what I need to know is--
(distracted by her cart)
Are those chiu-chao dumplings? May I?
(savoring a dumpling)
Pork, dried shrimp, peanuts, chives and
mushrooms in glutinous rice flour. Your
father could make a grown man cry.
RUBBIE arrives, 30, overweight and awkward, clearly dotes on
Mei. They make a strange couple.
This is Rubbie Wu, my fiancé. Also manager of
the dim sum.
You got a hell of a restaurant here.
Rubbie smiles at Mei--
I’m a lucky man in many ways.
(then)
Mr. Cod, right? You work upstairs.
Cuttlefish, beef balls and taro dumplings
every Sunday at noon.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
I’m sorry for your loss, both in the human and
gastronomic sense. Speaking of the talented
chef that was your father-- is it possible he
was also a degenerate gambler? I’m hearing he
was killed over a bet.
He didn’t have time for anything but work.
Least, as far as I know. My father and I
weren’t very close.
What about betting on the premises, between
employees maybe, or customers?
We’re just a dim sum restaurant. If Bao was
in trouble ‘cause of gambling? It didn’t
happen here.
OFF this...

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - BOOTH - NIGHT

lines.text: Ned and Chuck with Emerson.
Doesn’t sound like Mei’s too broken up over
dear old, dead Dad.
Didn’t waste a lotta tears. That said, I
poked around the restaurant and there’s no
basement, secret card rooms or the like.
Maybe Bao meant something else when he said he
lost a bet.
Maybe Bao had a pipe through his head and we’re
chasing smoke. Call you when I get a lead.
Emerson exits. Olive passes Ned and Chuck with a tray.
Dwight stopped by again. Didn’t say much.
Just the kind, warmhearted smile with the
crinkly eyes that say, “I wish I could find my
old friend, Ned’s dad, before I die alone.”
Olive moves on. Ned, off Chuck--
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED:
I know that face. It’s an “I’m still waiting
to hear why you won’t help your father’s
friend” face.
It’s a “you don’t read my face as well as you
think” face.
I keep my feelings about Dad behind a door
that’s been closed so long, it’s wallpapered
over and you can’t see the seams, which is how
I like it. Dwight showing up is like a corner
that’s peeling.
I see a peeling corner, I want to rip it off.
You wouldn’t if you knew what was underneath.
In my case, it’s a colorful mix of anger,
chronic distrust and misplaced guilt...
My mom’s been lying to me for three decades
about who she is. Me and her have a whole
heap of stink to work out, and I would if I
could, but I can’t. But you can, if you
could, and you should.
Ned takes out a small flip-pad and pen, writes--
CHUCK (CONT’D)
What is that?
My clue pad for writing down clues.
I love that you have a clue pad.
He hands her the paper--
It’s my father’s address. You can give it to
Dwight. That’s as much as I can do.
How long have you had this?
A while.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED: (2)
By “a while,” the Pie-Maker meant 20 years, 11
months, 3 weeks, 5 days and 6 hours...

scenes.heading: INT. LONGBOROUGH SCHOOL - DAY - FLASHBACK (RE-USE FROM “GIRTH”)

lines.text: Young Ned steps up to a POST MISTRESS at the Longborough School,
who hands Young Ned a “WE’VE MOVED” postcard.
...since he had gotten word, whilst away at
boarding school, that his father had moved on
and started a new family. Without him.
As Young Ned flips it over to a picture of a COZY HOUSE...
BACK TO SCENE
ANGLE - THE FRONT DOOR where an OLD CHINESE MAN has entered, now
looks around. Chuck approaches.
Can I help you?
(in Mandarin, with subtitles)
I’m Bao’s oldest friend, and I’ll tell you
what you need to know. Also I need change for
a dollar, I’m parked at a meter.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - BOOTH - MOMENTS LATER

lines.text: Chuck sits next to HUA JIANG and translates.
This is Hua Jiang, he overheard us at the
restaurant. He says there’s been illegal
gambling at the dim sum since they opened back
in Prohibition days.
As Hua Jiang continues talking...

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM RESTAURANT - DINING ROOM - SEPIA FLASHBACK (1920S)

lines.text: Several tables of gambling CHINESE MEN hold cigars and play
poker, dressed in period clothing. Women watch by their sides.
CHUCK (V.O.)
He says they would pull the shades and play
cards for money all night long. When your
luck was running, you’d have a woman on each
arm and all the milk you could drink.
As the men robustly toast with GLASSES OF MILK, one drinking out
of a booze-bottle full--
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
RETURN TO SCENE
“Milk”?
Might not be the right word. My Mandarin’s a
little rusty.
Hua Jiang continues...
BACK TO FLASHBACK
Chaos as 5 POLICE and a G-MAN (Fed) burst in waving GUNS. The
gamblers sweep their cards from the table, rush to hide milk or
flee--
CHUCK (V.O.)
This went on till the police finally caught on
and shut them down. But he says they always
found a way to keep the card game going.
BACK TO SCENE
He’s sure there’s still gambling there.

scenes.heading: INT. DIM SUM RESTAURANT - LOBBY - NIGHT

lines.text: Emerson, Chuck and Ned peer into the dining room.
Already searched the whole damn place.
There were gin joints in the ‘20s that used
underground passageways, or secret panels.
You had to know the password--
(off Ned)
What?
I was expecting Emerson to say something snarky.
Emerson has disappeared. As they stop to look:
NED (CONT’D)
Emerson?
Chuck notices TWO BLACK SHOES behind long drapes on the wall.
ANGLE - BEHIND THE DRAPES (OR VASE, AQUARIUM FISHTANK, ETC.)
Chuck and Ned join Emerson, who’s spying on a table.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 20.
CONTINUED:
Are we spying? I love spying.
Shh.
They all look at a LARGE, ROUND TABLE across the room. Simone
sits, dog beside her, alongside five HARD-LOOKING CHINESE MEN,
many of them sporting TATTOOS.
(spotting Simone)
Hey, isn’t that...?
Simone. The dog lady you dated. Is that why
we’re hiding?
We ain’t hiding and we didn’t date.
You wanted to.
And then I didn’t.
Why you didn’t?
No kidding, she is gorgeous.
There’s complicated issues in this situation
which you need to know nothing about ‘cept
that their complexity makes this shallow
conversation absurd.
Strange.
You calling my romantic life “strange”?
No. It’s strange that none of the people at
that table are eating.
ANGLE - THE TABLE
On the SIX DINERS, each with an array of small plates.
PUSHING DAISIES #205 "Dim Sum Lose Some" 08/11/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 21.
CONTINUED: (2)
As they continued to observe the diners who
were not dining, several unusual details
became apparent: all plates at the table were
covered with a bamboo lid.
